spec.name: Timoshenko cantilever with parabolic end shear (plane stress, fully clamped root)
spec.geometry: Rectangle [0, 48] x [-6, 6] (L = 48, D = 12), unit thickness, 2D plane stress. Edge x = 0 is fully clamped (u_x = u_y = 0). Edge x = 48 is loaded. Edges y = ±6 are traction-free. The corners (0, ±6) are where the clamped edge meets a traction-free edge.
spec.material: E = 3.0e7, nu = 0.3, plane stress. The problem gives only small-strain constants (isotropic linear elastic). The pipeline is for hyperelasticity, so a hyperelastic model would have to reduce to these constants (for example St. Venant–Kirchhoff or compressible neo-Hookean with mu = E/(2(1+nu)) and the matching plane-stress lambda). The model is not specified; see open_questions.
spec.loading: Dead traction on x = 48: t_y(y) = -(3P/(2D))(1 - 4y^2/D^2) with P = 1000, D = 12, and t_x = 0. Integrated over y in [-6, 6], this gives a net vertical force of -P = -1000, acting downward. There is no body force. The load is applied in one step or ramped, quasi-static.
qois: Vertical tip displacement u_y at (48, 0) (primary QoI)
Total strain energy / external work (secondary; converges despite the corner singularities)
Optional: region-averaged bending stress sigma_xx over a sub-domain away from x = 0 (e.g., x in [12, 36])
well_posedness: Boundary conditions: the full clamp at x = 0 removes all rigid-body modes, so the problem is well posed. This clamp is not the support condition of the Timoshenko–Goodier closed-form solution, which assumes the exact parabolic shear traction at x = 0 or point constraints at (0, 0). So the closed-form displacement field is not the exact solution of this boundary-value problem.

Singular features: at (0, ±6) a clamped edge meets a traction-free edge. This gives a weak stress singularity, so peak or pointwise stresses at the root will not converge under refinement. Tip displacement, strain energy and region averages away from the root are integral-type quantities and should converge. Global convergence rates may be reduced from the smooth-solution rates (Q4: O(h^2) L2, O(h) H1) unless the mesh is graded toward the corners.
Material stability: E > 0 and 0 < nu = 0.3 < 0.5, so the small-strain response is positive definite. Any hyperelastic model calibrated to these constants is stable near the reference state.

Load level vs. limit points: P/(E·D) is of order 1e-6. Beam theory gives a tip deflection of a few thousandths of a unit against L = 48, so strains are tiny and rotations are small. The response is essentially linear, with no buckling or limit points. The nonlinear and linear solutions should agree to within a negligible geometric-nonlinearity correction.

Locking: a fully integrated Q4 suffers from parasitic shear (shear locking) in bending-dominated problems on coarse meshes, especially with elements elongated along x. It still converges, but the pre-asymptotic tip deflection can be badly underestimated, and the refinement study should be started at meshes fine enough to be in the asymptotic range. Q8/Q9 or incompatible-mode/reduced-integration elements reduce this effect.
Traction consistency: the parabolic traction integrates exactly to P over the height, so the load is statically consistent.
open_questions: Which hyperelastic constitutive model, if any, is to be used (St. Venant–Kirchhoff, compressible neo-Hookean, ...)? Should a geometrically nonlinear solve be run, or is linear elasticity intended?

Should the reference be the Timoshenko–Goodier closed-form value? That value is consistent only with the matching root support, not a full clamp. Or should it be a mesh refinement family on the clamped problem, as assumed here? Is a reference tip deflection value supplied? None is given in the problem statement.
Which element is to be used? Q4 is assumed as the classic benchmark choice. Is it fully integrated, selectively reduced, or incompatible-mode (Q6/EAS), given shear locking in bending?
What are the mesh family and refinement ratio (e.g., 4x1, 8x2, 16x4, ... elements), and are the meshes uniform or graded toward the root corners?
Is the traction applied as a dead load (reference configuration) or a follower load? The difference is negligible at this load level but should be stated.
Is the tip displacement taken at the node at (48, 0)? That needs an even number of elements through the height; otherwise it must be interpolated.
What tolerance or acceptance criterion applies to the tip displacement (relative error, observed convergence order, GCI)?

steps.detail: The free-end load is a parabolically distributed shear traction t_y(y) = -(3P/(2D))(1 - 4y^2/D^2), which varies along the edge x = 48. The pipeline only supports constant traction per boundary segment, so this load cannot be represented exactly. Replacing it with piecewise-constant steps would be an unstated approximation. The geometry (rectangle [0,48]x[-6,6]), the clamped edge at x = 0, the material and the point of interest are all representable; only the end load is not.

sources.quote: A cantilever beam of length L = 48 and height D = 12
made of a material with E = 30000000 and nu = 0.3
carries a total shear force P = 1000 distributed parabolically over the height, t_y(y) = -(3P / (2D)) (1 - 4 y^2 / D^2)
The quantity of interest is the vertical tip displacement at (48, 0).

assumptions: cell_size = 6 is taken from the domain bounds (half-height 6). It divides both 48 and 12, so the rectangle is tiled exactly by 8 x 2 cells with j = -1 and 0 covering y in [-6, 6].

The clamped edge is modelled as fully fixed (u = v = 0 along x = 0), as the problem states. Note that the analytical Timoshenko solution uses a different, partial constraint at x = 0, so even with a supported load the FE result would not match the analytical tip deflection exactly.
The parabolic end traction is deliberately left out of bcs because it cannot be represented. The description is incomplete and must not be run as is.
